hypotheses.reasoning: auth-svc was rolled out to v4.30.0 at 03:57:03 (#2047). Its startup line (#2083) shows 'response serializer v2 enabled'. From that point, account-svc fails to decode auth-svc POST /tokens replies because the required 'status' field is missing; the payload only has id, state, updatedAt (#2200, #2231, #2330, #2346). account-svc therefore cannot issue tokens, and edge-proxy returns 502 on POST /login (#2185, #2262), with more 502s after. Before the deploy, auth-svc returned 200 OK responses and logins succeeded (#2044, #2045). The 502s are a symptom of the broken contract; the fault is the serializer change in v4.30.0. Other errors (S3 500s in template-svc, notify 500s, billing invoice checksum errors) are real but do not explain the login path.

billing-reconciler reports invoice_archive rows violating checksum constraints (partition 2019-Q*). This is a real data problem but it is not on the login path and does not match the timing of the 502s, which start at the auth-svc deploy. Ruled out as the cause of the login failures.

verdict.recommendedAction: Roll back auth-svc from v4.30.0 to v4.29.5 (or turn off response serializer v2) to restore the 'status' field in POST /tokens responses. Then confirm the edge-proxy 502 rate on POST /login drops below threshold. Follow up on the serializer contract and the unrelated template-svc S3 failures and billing checksum errors.
